purpose: Determine which Irish legal regime, statutory instrument, case-law framework and temporal version applies to a classified property question before legal effect is stated.
selection_rules: The law applicable to a historical event must not be selected solely from the current consolidated text.
An amendment date is not automatically the date on which the amended provision became operative.
A repeal does not automatically erase legal consequences that occurred while the earlier regime applied.
Where commencement or transitional provisions matter, they must be resolved before stating the legal effect.
Related regimes must be retained where one event produces effects under more than one legal framework.
Case law must be matched to the relevant legal provision, date and issue rather than used as a substitute for the statute.
guardrails: Never infer the applicable historical law from today's wording alone.
Never treat a case citation as proof that every proposition in the case applies to the present question.
Never collapse different legal regimes merely because they concern the same property.
If the applicable temporal version cannot be established, mark the legal regime unresolved.
